Subject: Post-call recap: Data retention, deletion SLAs & log/backups (Amaya)

Hi Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from our call:
- Amaya needs clear deletion SLAs for customer data (primary stores) and audit log retention windows for compliance reviews.
- You indicated potential HIPAA applicability for a subset of records and that GDPR data subject requests are a requirement.
- You asked about SOC 2 status and whether Redwood will accept vendor questionnaire (we offered a short vendor security questionnaire).
- Backup retention/restore windows: you asked how long backups are retained and whether those are covered by the same deletion SLA.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share Redwood’s retention and deletion SLA table (attached) and our SOC 2 Type II report.
2) Neha can kick off the vendor security questionnaire and answer HIPAA/GDPR specifics.
3) If helpful, we can loop in Legal for any contract language on data subject rights / deletion confirmation.

Please confirm if the items above reflect your understanding and which two people from your side should be included on the vendor questionnaire.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB)

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. That matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side before Neha kicks off the questionnaire: 

1) SOC 2: we typically ask for the date range covered and whether there are any outstanding exceptions. If your report contains those details, great — otherwise a short bullet is fine.
2) Deletion SLA: for our risk team we need to understand the distinction between deletion from primary storage vs. backups — specifically: is deletion from backups guaranteed within the same SLA window or are backups considered a separate retention window with separate controls?
3) Logs: we retain audit logs for 12 months internally; are Redwood’s application and access logs configurable per-customer and what are the default retention periods?

People to include on the questionnaire: me (alex.thompson@amaya.com) and Priya Das (priya.das@amaya.com, Engineering Security).

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Thompson

Hi Alex / Marissa — thanks, Alex, for the detail. I started the questionnaire (attached a short vendor security questionnaire draft) and answered the high-level items. Quick answers inline below; full responses are attached and I'll send the formal questionnaire to Alex + Priya this afternoon.

SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. Report period: 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31. No outstanding exceptions noted in the final report. We have the redacted report attached (Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf).

Deletion SLAs / backups: Our standard deletion SLA for primary customer data is 30 days from request (we remove from primary stores and metadata indices). Backups are retained for disaster recovery for a default of 90 days; backups are indexed separately and are not immediately purged on a standard deletion request unless covered by a contractual commitment. For enterprise contracts we can negotiate an expedited backup purge and provide a deletion attestation — that typically requires an enterprise commitment and operational coordination (we document the process in the contract appendix).

Logs: Default application and access log retention is 180 days. We can offer configurable retention windows (30/90/180/365) for Dedicated/Private customers depending on plan and legal requirements. For hosted customers, custom retention is available via Redwood Optimize + a contract addendum.

Attachments: vendor-questionnaire-draft.docx (DOCX, 45KB) — will send the completed questionnaire to Alex + Priya after internal review.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

- Can you confirm the process and timeline for a contractual expedited backup purge? Who on Redwood operations is the point of contact and what SLAs do you typically commit to for that?
- For the deletion attestation: can you share a sample attestation template or describe the minimum fields (date of request, data identifiers, confirmation of purge from backups, signature) so our legal team can draft corresponding language?

If you can send the sample attestation and an outline of the expedited purge process, we can move to a short legal review. Thanks — Alex
